p01.text: You finish work. You get home. You sit down.
p01.heard: You finish work, you get home, you sit down,

p02.text: And you start a second job.
p02.heard: and you start a second job.

p03.text: By day, you dive into a hole in the ocean and spear fish until your oxygen runs out. By night, you serve them as sushi until closing time.
p03.heard: By day, you dive into a hole in the ocean and spear fish until your oxygen runs out. By night, you serve them as sushi until closing time.

p04.text: Nobody pays you. Nobody makes you.
p04.heard: Nobody pays you, nobody makes you.

p05.text: Dave the Diver has sold more than ten million copies, according to the studio.
p05.heard: Dave the Diver has sold more than 10 million copies, according to the studio.

p06.text: Ten million people... clocking in. After clocking out.
p06.heard: 10 million people, clocking in after clocking out.

p07.text: And in 2023, Steam players voted it their award for "Sit Back and Relax."
p07.heard: in 2023, steam players voted at their award for sit back and relax.

p09.text: Meet Dave. He doesn't look like a hero. Round. Easygoing. A wetsuit that has seen things. Even the developers say his body isn't typical for a diver.
p09.heard: Meet Dave, he doesn't look like a hero. Round, easygoing, a wetsuit that has seen things, even the developers say his body isn't typical for a diver.

p10.text: Dave is on vacation. Then his old friend Cobra calls, with the promise of sushi.
p10.heard: Dave is on vacation, then his old friend Cobra calls with the promise of sushi.

p11.text: So Dave ends his vacation. Immediately. Because Dave really likes sushi.
p11.heard: So Dave ends his vacation, immediately, because Dave really likes sushi.

p12.text: There's just one detail. The restaurant has no fish. Dave is the fish supply.
p12.heard: There's just one detail, the restaurant has no fish, Dave is the fish supply.

p13.text: One player called it "the shortest supply chain in the world." It's one guy. Holding a harpoon.
p13.heard: One player called it the shortest supply chain in the world, it's one guy holding a harpoon.

p14.text: And it gets worse. Cobra keeps signing contracts for him. An archaeologist. A weapons nerd. A reporter. Without asking.
p14.heard: And it gets worse, Cobra keeps signing contracts for him, an archaeologist, a weapons nerd, a reporter without asking.

p15.text: You probably have a Cobra. The friend who already told everyone you'd help them move. The boss who said yes for you, in a meeting you weren't in.
p15.heard: You probably have a Cobra, the friend who already told everyone you'd help them move, the boss who said yes for you in a meeting you weren't in.

p16.text: Dave could leave. He doesn't. Hold on to that.
p16.heard: could leave, he doesn't hold on to that.

p17.text: The easy answer is that it's cozy. Pixel art. Gentle music. A little sushi bar by the sea.
p17.heard: The easy answer is that it's cozy, pixel art, gentle music, a little sushi bar by the sea.

p18.text: But it isn't only cozy. The deep has sharks. A hermit crab that lives in a dump truck. A squid the size of a bus. And your oxygen is also your health. Get bitten, and the tank drops.
p18.heard: But it isn't only cozy, the deep has sharks, a hermit crab that lives in a dump truck, a squid the size of a bus, and your oxygen is also your health, get bitten and the tank drops.

p19.text: Danger below. Rice above. Which is also a fair description of most Mondays.
p19.heard: Danger below, rice above, which is also a fair description of most Mondays.

p20.text: And cozy alone doesn't explain it. Plenty of games let you relax. Some even let you quit the office. Dave hands you a better shift.
p20.heard: And cozy alone doesn't explain it, plenty of games let you relax, some even let you quit the office, Dave hands you a better shift.

p20b.text: So why does a shift feel better than a nap?
p20b.heard: So why does a shift feel better than a nap?

p22.text: Every day, Dave drops into the Blue Hole. And every dive, it's different. New layout. New fish. New trouble.
p22.heard: every day Dave drops into the blue hole, and every dive it's different, new layout, new fish, new trouble.

p23.text: And every dive has an ending you can see. A gauge. When the oxygen runs out, they pull you up, and you keep one thing. One.
p23.heard: And every dive has an ending you can see, a gauge, when the oxygen runs out they pull you up and you keep one thing, one.

p24.text: Now think about your own workday. When did it last end? Not "end of day." Actually end. The email at ten at night says no.
p24.heard: Now think about your own work day, when did it last end, not end of day, actually end, the email at 10 at night says no.

p25.text: Dave's work has a clock you can see. Yours mostly has a phone.
p25.heard: Dave's work has a clock you can see, yours mostly has a phone.

p26.text: And when Dave gets better, you can see that too. His air tank goes from ninety bar to four hundred and eighty. His cargo box, from nine kilos to a hundred and eighty-five. His suit, from forty meters deep to eight hundred.
p26.heard: And when Dave gets better you can see that too, his air tank goes from 90 bar to 480, his cargo box from 9 kilos to 185, his suit from 40 meters deep to 800.

p27.text: He doesn't get a promotion. He gets a bigger tank.
p27.heard: He doesn't get a promotion, he gets a bigger tank.

p28.text: Out here, getting better at your job mostly means... more job.
p28.heard: Out here getting better at your job mostly means more job.

p29.text: Then the sun goes down, and the second half begins. Bancho Sushi.
p29.heard: Then the sun goes down and the second half begins, Bancho Sushi.

p30.text: Bancho is the chef. A man so serious about fish that, according to the game, he lost a job at a five-star hotel over a food critic and a whole roasted shark head.
p30.heard: Bancho is the chef, a man so serious about fish that according to the game he lost a job at a 5 star hotel over a food critic and a whole roasted shark head.

p31.text: Bancho's new recipes come with anime cutscenes. Knives flash. A petal falls. Somewhere, a catfish looks terrified.
p31.heard: Bancho's new recipes come with anime cutscenes, knives flash, a petal falls, somewhere a catfish looks terrified.

p32.text: And Dave runs the floor. Tea. Wasabi. Plates. Faster, faster. Until closing. And then the game gives you a score for the night. Even your phone has an app for it, Cooksta, where the followers are people you actually fed.
p32.heard: And Dave runs the floor, tea, wasabi, plates, faster faster until closing. And then the game gives you a score for the night, even your phone has an app for it cooksta where the followers are people you actually fed.

p33.text: Here's the part that matters. The fish you speared at noon... is on a plate at eight. And somebody eats it.
p33.heard: Here's the part that matters, the fish you speared at noon is on a plate at 8 and somebody eats it.

p34.text: Most of us make things nobody ever sees. A report goes into a folder. The folder goes into another folder.
p34.heard: Most of us make things nobody ever sees. A report goes into a folder, the folder goes into another folder.

p35.text: The director split the day in two so you could focus on each half. And so you'd feel like you were "preparing dinner for customers."
p35.heard: The director split the day in two so you could focus on each half and so you'd feel like you were preparing dinner for customers.

p36.text: Not a task. A dinner. For someone.
p36.heard: Not a task, a dinner for someone.

p37.text: And the customers aren't the only ones waiting.
p37.heard: And the customers aren't the only ones waiting.

p38.text: Duff, the weapons guy, who loves his anime idols louder than any adult is supposed to love anything.
p38.heard: Duff the weapons guy who loves his anime idols louder than any adult is supposed to love anything.

p39.text: Otto, the farmer in the straw hat, who has been away from home a long time, and wants to fix his life before he calls.
p39.heard: Otto the farmer in the straw hat who has been away from home a long time and wants to fix his life before he calls.

p40.text: And deep under the Blue Hole, a whole village of Sea People, who need Dave too.
p40.heard: And deep under the blue hole, a whole village of sea people who need Dave too.

p41.text: Every one of them needs Dave to do the one thing they can't.
p41.heard: Every one of them needs Dave to do the one thing they can't.

p42.text: Being needed by four thousand people is called a job. Being needed by five is called a family. Or, apparently, a sushi bar.
p42.heard: Being needed by 4 ,000 people is called a job, being needed by 5 is called a family, or apparently a sushi bar.

p43.text: And yes, some players say the game never stops handing you chores. A fish farm. A rice paddy. Seahorse racing. Fair. Dave never says no either.
p43.heard: And yes, some players say the game never stops handing you chores, a fish farm, a rice paddy, seahorse racing, fair, Dave never says no either.

p44.text: Which brings us back to Cobra. Dave could leave. He never does. Because somewhere along the way, the contracts became friends.
p44.heard: Which brings us back to Cobra, Dave could leave, he never does, because somewhere along the way the contracts became friends.

p45.text: So... why do millions of people come home from work to work two jobs?
p45.heard: So why do millions of people come home from work to work two jobs?

p46.text: Because it was never about working more. It's about work that finally fits in a day.
p46.heard: Because it was never about working more, it's about work that finally fits in a day.

p47.text: It ends. You can see it. And someone is glad you came.
p47.heard: It ends you can see it and someone is glad you came.

p48.text: The idea came from a real restaurant on Jeju Island, in South Korea. In the director's words, "the owner caught fish in the morning, and cooked them for dinner."
p48.heard: idea came from a real restaurant on Jeju Island in South Korea. In the director's words, the owner caught fish in the morning and cooked them for dinner.

p49.text: One person. One day. A job you can hold in your hands.
p49.heard: One person, one day, a job you can hold in your hands.

p50.text: Then you put the controller down. Tomorrow, the real job is still there. Still no oxygen gauge. Still no score at closing time.
p50.heard: Then you put the controller down, tomorrow the real job is still there, still no oxygen gauge, still no score at closing time.

p51.text: But tonight, for an hour, you got to clock out like Dave. Done by closing time. Somebody glad you came.
p51.heard: But tonight for an hour you got to clock out like Dave, done by closing time, somebody glad you came.

p52.text: Maybe that's what we're really playing. Not a second job. The first one... the way it was supposed to feel.
p52.heard: Maybe that's what we're really playing, not a second job, the first one, the way it was supposed to feel.

p53.text: So what would your second shift be? And what game deserves a "why?" next? Tell me in the comments.
p53.heard: So what would your second shift be and what game deserves a Y next? Tell me in the comments.
